description: The NVMe cold tier below the host KV tier (docs/tp4-kv-nvme.md): a raw-namespace spill of the host tier's evictions and of the checkpoint store's, restored on a miss in both host stores, so a returning session's KV stays warm for up to a day since its last use (owner decisions 2026-10-21: all tenants, TTL 1 day) and comes back in about a second or two instead of a 75 to 145 s cold re-prefill. QWEN_PREFIX_NVME=1 with QWEN_PREFIX_NVME_DEVICE and the required QWEN_PREFIX_NVME_RETENTION_ACK=1, Write-through (QWEN_PREFIX_NVME_SPILL=through, idle 0) is the default and a graceful stop drains the writer queue (QWEN_PREFIX_NVME_DRAIN_S, default 4 s); the stored KV survives a deploy (the fingerprint is KV_EPOCH, the model, the drafter, the KV layout and three byte-defining switches, not the image or the profile name). The drive must be an Opal self-encrypting drive with locking enabled and unlocked (QWEN_PREFIX_NVME_REQUIRE_SED, on by default; 0 is a gate's own), TRIM is on by default. Never run on a card.

smoke.what: NVMe cold tier below the host KV tier (the scheduler graft's install line; a REFUSED line, the zero-retention guard, logs no 'on' line and so fails the arm too)

image_files.reason: the NVMe tier: flags, layout fingerprint, checkpoint codec, restore backends, the spill writer; qwen_prefix_registry and the contract import it only when a QWEN_PREFIX_NVME name is set
the raw-namespace object store under it: superblocks, journal, snapshots, extent allocator, O_DIRECT IO

card_jobs: none written here: docs/tp4-kv-nvme.md section 12 is the plan (R1 the drive re-probe, D0 the drive bench, A1 the audited attach on the format twin, E1 the encryption check, N1 exactness at 64k/128k/254k, N2 timed restore, N3 spill under eight live seats, N4 the concurrent restore ABAB, N5 restart persistence and the stop, N6 write-through, U1 the UPGRADE gate across two images, Z the reset). Built on tp4/kv-nvme-2: the runner keys C2_NVME_DEVICE and C2_P2PMEM, the generated nvme twins (make_nvme_profiles) and the prefix gate's nvme-exact, nvme-timed, nvme-concurrent, nvme-concurrent-whole and nvme-restart plans
notes: FLAGS. All default off and strict (qwen_kv_nvme.parse); the switch needs the host tier, the device and QWEN_PREFIX_NVME_RETENTION_ACK=1. A traffic profile may name QWEN_PREFIX_NVME=1 only under an owner traffic waiver that names it (serving_c2_contract.NVME_WAIVABLE_LEVERS); the audit, the format override, the command directory and the zero-retention override stay a gate's. THE GATE TWINS ARE GENERATED (make_nvme_profiles.py: the ship-7 candidate and its audit twin plus these names, gate only, the host share cut to STORE_GIB + 4; a format twin for the first gate), and the prefix gate's nvme plans judge every arm served on one (c2_prefix_gate.nvme_findings). The tier does not start (a REFUSED line, nvme_refused_zero_retention) on a node that looks zero-retention unless QWEN_PREFIX_NVME_ALLOW_ON_ZERO_RETENTION=1; a drive that cannot be opened logs UNAVAILABLE, and one that vanishes at run time logs DEVICE LOST once (nvme_device_lost); the host tier serves in both cases. The tier refuses to open a drive that is not shown to be encrypted (a REFUSED line, nvme_refused_not_encrypted); a gate profile sets QWEN_PREFIX_NVME_REQUIRE_SED=0 until the drive is set up.
